title: Mastering Markdown & Plain Text ✍️
description: Learn to produce beautifully formatted documents, emails, and reports by commanding markdown and plain text structure.

slides.title: Markdown as Universal Format 🌐
slides.content:
# Why Markdown?

Markdown is the lingua franca of modern text – used in GitHub, Notion, Slack, and most LLM chat interfaces. When you ask for markdown, you get:
- **Headers** (`#`, `##`) for hierarchy.
- **Bold** and *italic* for emphasis.
- **Lists** (ordered and unordered).
- **Code blocks**.
- **Links and images**.

Most LLMs natively understand markdown and will output it when prompted.

slides.title: How to Request Markdown 📝
slides.content:
## Simple Phrases That Work

Use explicit instructions:
- `Output in markdown format.`
- `Use markdown headers and bullet points.`
- `Format your response as a markdown document.`

Even better, give a skeleton:
> `Provide the answer in the following markdown structure: ## Title, ### Subtitle, - bullet 1, - bullet 2`

The more specific the requested structure, the more faithfully the model will reproduce it.

quizData.question: Which phrase is most likely to result in a well‑structured markdown response?

options.text: "Output in markdown with ## for main points, and bullet lists for details."

quizData.explanation: Explicit instructions with the desired markdown tokens leave no ambiguity.

slides.title: Crafting Plain Text with Structure 📋
slides.content:
## Even Without Markdown, You Can Control Layout

Sometimes you need a specific plain text format, like an email or a log entry. Use instructions like:
- `Start with 'Subject:', then the body.`
- `Use numbered lines.`
- `Separate sections with '---'.`

Example:
> `Write a polite follow‑up email. Format: Subject: [title], then a blank line, then the body.`

You can also request templates with placeholders:
> `Create a meeting agenda template with placeholders [Date], [Attendees], [Topics].`

slides.title: Markdown Request Example 📄
slides.content:
**Prompt:**
```
Create a daily stand‑up update for a software team. Use markdown:
## Accomplishments
- [List items]
## Plans for Today
- [List items]
## Blockers
- [List items, or 'None']
```

**Output:**
```
## Accomplishments
- Merged login feature PR
- Fixed cart bug

## Plans for Today
- Start on payment integration
- Code review for team

## Blockers
- Waiting on API keys from DevOps
```
slides.codeSnippet: Requested markdown structure yields a ready‑to‑paste update.

quizData.question: To make the AI output a specific email format, the best approach is:

options.text: Provide a template with field names like 'Subject:', 'Body:', etc.

quizData.explanation: Providing an explicit template ensures the output matches your required structure exactly.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Combine Markdown with Other Formats

You can ask for JSON inside a markdown code block:
> `Provide the data as a JSON object inside a markdown code block labeled json.`

This gives you both human‑readable formatting and machine‑extractability.
